# smbact-cli reference

`smbact-cli 2.0.0`, built from smbact-app 93372cf. The help text below is verbatim.

## smbact-cli 

```text
Applies SMBAct's layout actions (halves, thirds, fourths, quarters, sixths, eighths, center, move, maximize, restore) to the frontmost window, with SMBAct's repeated-press cycling. Reads SMBAct's settings read-only. While SMBAct runs, the window commands and `mcp serve` go through it (one repeat state, its rules); --standalone keeps them here.

Usage: smbact-cli [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  run           Apply an action to the frontmost window, or to --window-id (e.g. `run left-half`)
  actions       List the supported actions, their repeat cycles and the profile's hotkeys
  windows       List the open windows (ids for --window-id, focus, close)
  displays      List the displays
  focus         Bring a window to the front (un-minimizes it): ID from `windows`, or `active`
  close         Close a window (like its close button), or with --app every window of its application
  minimize-all  Minimize all windows (black-listed apps are skipped)
  mcp           Local MCP server for AI assistants, and its settings (shared with the app)
  license       The license smbact-cli honours: SMBAct's own (read-only), or an offline license
  place         Place one window or several at any geometry, through the running SMBAct (`place --help` lists the flags)
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --settings-dir <DIR>
          SMBAct settings directory [default: the app's userData — macOS ~/Library/Application Support/SMBAct, Linux ~/.config/SMBAct]

      --app-data-dir <DIR>
          The app data dir of an SMBAct started with --app-data-dir=DIR (a development run): the settings dir is DIR/SMBAct. Also where the CLI looks for that SMBAct to hand over to

      --standalone
          Never hand over to a running SMBAct: this process does everything, as when SMBAct is not running (docs/cli-handoff.md)

      --profile <ID>
          Profile code (a directory under <settings-dir>/profiles) [default: settings.json activeProfile]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## smbact-cli run

```text
Apply an action to the frontmost window, or to --window-id (e.g. `run left-half`)

Usage: smbact-cli run [OPTIONS] <ACTION>

Arguments:
  <ACTION>  Action: short name (`left-half`) or full id (`active-application:actions:left-half`)

Options:
      --dry-run             Print the window, display, chosen action and target frame; move nothing, write no state
      --settings-dir <DIR>  SMBAct settings directory [default: the app's userData — macOS ~/Library/Application Support/SMBAct, Linux ~/.config/SMBAct]
      --app-data-dir <DIR>  The app data dir of an SMBAct started with --app-data-dir=DIR (a development run): the settings dir is DIR/SMBAct. Also where the CLI looks for that SMBAct to hand over to
      --window <X,Y,W,H>    (with --dry-run) Use this window frame instead of the frontmost window: X,Y,W,H (top-left origin)
      --display <RECT>      (with --dry-run) Use this display instead of the real ones: X,Y,W,H[,VX,VY,VW,VH] (frame and optional visible frame). Repeat for several displays; the first is main
      --standalone          Never hand over to a running SMBAct: this process does everything, as when SMBAct is not running (docs/cli-handoff.md)
      --profile <ID>        Profile code (a directory under <settings-dir>/profiles) [default: settings.json activeProfile]
      --state-file <PATH>   Repeat-state file [default: $TMPDIR/smbact-cli.state]
      --no-repeat           Ignore repeated presses (always apply the pressed action)
      --window-id <ID>      Act on this window instead of the frontmost one: ID from `windows` ("<pid>:<window>")
  -h, --help                Print help
```

## smbact-cli mcp

```text
Local MCP server for AI assistants, and its settings (shared with the app)

Commands:
  serve     Serve MCP: stdio (default; for `command`-style client configs) or --http on 127.0.0.1
  status    Settings, token state, whether SMBAct runs and whether the port is taken
  config    Show the settings, or change them: KEY=VALUE … (enabled, port, require-token, confirm-close, tool.window_action|focus_window|minimize_all|close_window|move_window_to_desktop| set_window_frame|move_window_to_display|place_windows = on/off)
  token     Print the access token; --regenerate makes a new one (old clients stop working)
  snippets  Client configuration snippets (Claude Code, Cursor/.mcp.json, Claude Desktop; HTTP and stdio)
```

```text

Usage: smbact-cli license issue-offline [OPTIONS] --key <KEY> --device <DEVICE>

Options:
      --key <KEY>           The license key
      --settings-dir <DIR>  SMBAct settings directory [default: the app's userData — macOS ~/Library/Application Support/SMBAct, Linux ~/.config/SMBAct]

      --days <DAYS>         Days (1-3650); default the longest the license allows
      --standalone          Never hand over to a running SMBAct: this process does everything, as when SMBAct is not running (docs/cli-handoff.md)
      --out <OUT>           Also write the license text to this file (0600)
      --profile <ID>        Profile code (a directory under <settings-dir>/profiles) [default: settings.json activeProfile]
      --armor               Print (and save) the mail-safe form: a BEGIN/END SMBACT LICENSE block of base64
  -h, --help                Print help
```

## smbact-cli place

```text
Place one window or several at any geometry (SMBAct must be running; it does the work).

Usage: smbact-cli place [FLAGS] [--then FLAGS]... [--json]

Positions and sizes refer to the work area of the window's display by default (--area work); lengths are integers (native units), <n>dip, <p>%, <a>/<b> or rel:<value>. --then starts the next placement; request flags (--dry-run, --strict, --tolerance, --timeout-ms) may stand anywhere. With --dry-run, --window X,Y,W,H and --display X,Y,W,H[,VX,VY,VW,VH][@scale] simulate a desktop. --keep-state = --state keep. --json prints the result object.

Placement flags:
  --window-id        A window id from list_windows ("<pid>:<handle>"), or "active" for the frontmost window when the request started (the default when no other target key is given). With other target keys it is an assertion: the window must also match them.
  --app              The app name as list_windows reports it: exact, case-insensitive ("Code" does not match "Xcode").
  --bundle-id        macOS: the app's bundle id; Linux and Windows: the window class (list_windows class). Exact, case-insensitive.
  --title            The title contains this text (case-insensitive).
  --title-regex      The title matches this regular expression (case-sensitive; "(?i)" at the start ignores case). No look-around, backreferences or named groups.
  --pid              The owning process id (the part of the window id before the colon).
  --nth              The Nth match, front to back, 1-based. Above the number of matches it is "no match".
  --on-multiple      [first|error|all] Several windows match: the frontmost (first, with the warning multiple_matches), an error (ambiguous_target), or all.
  --if-missing       [error|skip] No window matches: fail the placement (window_not_found), or skip it.
  --wait-ms          Wait up to this long for a matching window to appear (counts against timeout_ms).
  --x                Left edge, from the area's left edge (with anchor: an inward offset). A length: an integer or "<n>px" (native units, as list_windows), "<n>dip" (device-independent), "<p>%" or "<a>/<b>" (of the area), or "rel:<value>" (relative to the current frame).
  --y                Top edge, from the area's top edge (with anchor: an inward offset). A length: an integer or "<n>px" (native units, as list_windows), "<n>dip" (device-independent), "<p>%" or "<a>/<b>" (of the area), or "rel:<value>" (relative to the current frame).
  --width            Width. A length: an integer or "<n>px" (native units, as list_windows), "<n>dip" (device-independent), "<p>%" or "<a>/<b>" (of the area), or "rel:<value>" (relative to the current frame).
  --height           Height. A length: an integer or "<n>px" (native units, as list_windows), "<n>dip" (device-independent), "<p>%" or "<a>/<b>" (of the area), or "rel:<value>" (relative to the current frame).
  --frame            "x,y,width,height" in one string, e.g. "0,0,60%,100%"; an empty item keeps that component.
  --area             [work|full|screen] What positions and fractions refer to: the work area of the display (without menu bar, Dock, taskbar, panels), the full display, or the screen (absolute coordinates as list_windows reports them; no display, anchor, grid, dip or %).
  --display          Which display: current (the window's), an index from list_displays, main, active, cursor, next, prev, "name:<name>", "id:<id>", or a name. Alone (no geometry) it moves the window there, keeping its place and size relative to the work area.
  --anchor           [top-left|top|top-right|left|center|right|bottom-left|bottom|bottom-right] Attach the window to this point of the area; x and y become inward offsets (missing ones are 0).
  --pivot            [top-left|top|top-right|left|center|right|bottom-left|bottom|bottom-right] When only the size changes: the point of the current frame that stays put.
  --grid             "<cols>x<rows>" (1-64 each): a grid over the area; needs cell.
  --cell             "col,row[,colspan,rowspan]", 0-based: the grid cells the window covers.
  --gap              Space between grid cells: px or dip, 0-10000.
  --margin           Inset of the area on all four sides: px or dip, 0-10000.
  --min-width        Clamp the resolved width up to this (a length, no rel:).
  --min-height       Clamp the resolved height up to this (a length, no rel:).
  --max-width        Clamp the resolved width down to this (a length, no rel:).
  --max-height       Clamp the resolved height down to this (a length, no rel:).
  --fit              [none|move|shrink] Keep the frame inside the area: move it in, or shrink it first and then move it in.
  --allow-offscreen  Lift the reachability guard (a frame whose title bar cannot be grabbed is refused with target_offscreen).
  --state            [normalize|keep] normalize: leave fullscreen, un-minimize, un-maximize first (listed in state_changes); keep: refuse a window that is not normal (invalid_window_state).
  --desktop          [in-place|refuse] A window on a desktop that is not showing: place it where it is if the OS can (macOS cannot: window_on_other_desktop), or refuse it.

Request flags:
  --strict           A frame outside the tolerance counts as a failure (code constraint), not as adjusted.
  --tolerance        Native units a frame may be off and still count as exact.
  --dry-run          Resolve and report (status would_place), move nothing.
  --timeout-ms       The whole request; a placement still running then fails with timeout, the rest are not_attempted.

Exit codes: 0 applied or dry run, 1 failed, 2 usage or invalid request, 3 partial, 65 no license.
Examples:
  smbact-cli place --app Safari --frame 0,0,60%,100%
```
